Rashi on Nedarim 24a:1:1.hebrew: הרי זה יכול - המודר להתיר נדרו בעצמו שלא ע"פ חכם, שיכול לומר לו המודר: כלום אמרת ליתן לבני כך וכך אלא בשביל כבודי:
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:1:1.english: This [one] can - [That is,] the one prohibited by the vow [can] dissolve his vow by himself without a Sage, for the one prohibited by the vow can say to him: "Did you say to give my son such-and-such [for any reason] other than for my honor?"

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:1:2.hebrew: זהו כבודי - יותר שלא אקבל, שאיני צריך, וכבר הותר הנדר:
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:1:2.english: This is my honor - [It is] more [honorable] that I not accept [it], for I do not need [it], and the vow is already dissolved.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:2:1.hebrew: מני אי רבי אליעזר בן יעקב - אע"ג דלא אמר זהו כבודי, יותר בטל, דנדרי זירוזין הוא:
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:2:1.english: Whose [opinion is this]? If [it is] Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov - Even though he did not say, "This is my honor," it is all the more void, for it is [among] vows of exhortation.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:2:2.hebrew: אלא לאו רבנן היא - דסברי דלא הוי נדרי זירוזין, וש"מ פליגי:
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:2:2.english: Rather, is it not [the opinion of] the Rabbis - Who hold that it is not [a case of] vows of exhortation, and conclude from it [that] they disagree.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:3:1.hebrew: לעולם רבי אליעזר בן יעקב היא - הא מתני':
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:3:1.english: Actually, it is [according to] Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov - [referring to] this Mishnah:

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:3:2.hebrew: ומודה ר' אליעזר בן יעקב בהאי דנדר הוי - ולא זירוזין, דודאי משום נדר ממש קא"ל, דאמר ליה: לאו כלבא אנא כו':
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:3:2.english: And Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov concedes in this [case] that it is a vow - And not [mere] encouragement, for he certainly says [this] to him for the sake of an actual vow, as he says to him: "I am not a dog," etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:4:1.hebrew: וחכ"א אף זה - נודר יכול להתיר, שיכול לומר לו: הריני מחזיק לך טובה כאילו התקבלתי ממך, לפיכך אינו נדר:
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:4:1.english: And the Sages say: Even this [person] - [The] one who takes the vow can dissolve [it], for he can say to him: I am grateful to you as though I have received [it] from you; therefore, it is not a vow.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:5:1.hebrew: אי ר"א בן יעקב נדרי זירוזין הוו - שמזרזו ומדירו כדי שיתן לו כך וכך, אע"ג דלא אמר התקבלתי הוי בטל, דנדרי זירוזין הוו:
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:5:1.english: If Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov, they are vows of exhortation - For he exhorts him and imposes a vow upon him so that he will give him such-and-such; even though he did not say "I have received [it]," [the vow] is void, because they are vows of exhortation.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:5:2.hebrew: אלא לאו רבנן היא - דסברי דלא הוו נדרי זירוזין, אלמא פליגי:
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:5:2.english: Rather, is it not [the opinion of] the Rabbis - Who hold that they are not vows of exhortation; thus, they disagree.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:6:1.hebrew: לעולם ר"א בן יעקב היא - הא מתני':
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:6:1.english: Actually, it is Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov - [i.e.,] this Mishnah.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:6:2.hebrew: ומודה - דהאי לא הוה נדרי זירוזין אלא נדר ממש, ולהכי אי אמר "התקבלתי" לא הוי נדר:
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:6:2.english: And [Rabbi Eliezer] concedes - that this is not [a case of] vows of incitement, rather an actual vow, and therefore if he says, "I have received [it]," it is not a vow.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:6:3.hebrew: משום דאמר ליה לאו מלכא כו':
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:6:3.english: Because he says to him, "I am not a king," etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:7:1.hebrew: מני אי ר"א בן יעקב נדרי זירוזין הוו - המדיר חברו שיאכל עמו, ואפי' לא חלה, מותר:
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:7:1.english: Whose [opinion is this]? If [it is] Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, they are vows of exhortation - [Namely,] one who imposes a vow upon his friend that he should eat with him, and even if he did not become sick, it is permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:7:2.english: Rather, is it not [the opinion of] the Rabbis - and they disagree, [holding] that they are not vows of exhortation.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:8:1.hebrew: לעולם ר"א בן יעקב היא - ומודה דלאו נדרי זירוזין הוו:
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:8:1.english: Actually, it is [the view of] Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov - and he concedes that they are not vows of exhortation.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:8:2.english: Do you think that the host made [the guest] vow - For that is vows of exhortation.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:8:3.hebrew: לא, זמינא הוא דאדריה למזמנא, דאמר ליה: מזמנת לי בהדך? אמר ליה: אין. נדר זה קבל עליך, ונדר, וחלה הוא - המזומן; הא לא חלה, הוי נדר גמור:
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:8:3.english: No, [it is] the guest who caused the host to vow, for he said to him: "Are you inviting me with you?" He said to him: "Yes." [The guest said:] "Accept this vow upon yourself," and he [the host] vowed, and he fell ill - [this refers to] the invited guest. Had he not fallen ill, it would be a full-fledged vow.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:9:1.hebrew: יתר על כן - על אותו שאמר במשנה, אמר ר"א בן יעקב האומר לחבירו קונם שאיני נהנה לך כו':
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:9:1.english: More than this - [More] than that which he stated in the Mishnah, Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov said: One who says to his friend, "Konam that I will not benefit from you," etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:9:2.hebrew: והלה הקפיד כנגדו - אף על גב שפירש לו הכל, ואע"פ שהקפיד כנגדו, אף אלו נדרי זירוזין ומותר:
Rashi on Nedarim 24a:9:2.english: And the other became irritated at him - Even though he specified everything to him, and even though [the other] became irritated at him, these too are vows of exhortation, and it is permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 24a:9:3.english: And the Sages did not concede to him - That [this] should be vows of exhortation.

Tosafot on Nedarim 24a:8:1.hebrew: מי סברת דאדריה מזמנא לזמינא לא זמינא אדריה למזמנא אמר ליה מזמנת לי אמר ליה אין - פירוש: "כן, אני רוצה לזמן אותך". וא"ל זמינא למזמנא: "דור עליך שאתה מזמן לי". ונדר — פירוש: נדר מזמנא ואמר: "קונם פירות עלי אם אין אני מזמן אותך". ולא הוו נדרי זירוזין, משום דדוקא היכא שהמזומן מסרב ומזמן מפציר בו ומזרזו לאכול משלו — התם שייך נדרי זרוזין; אבל כאן אין צריך לזרז המזומן לאכול, שהרי אדרבה, המזומן מבקש מן המזמן שידור על כך שיזמנהו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 24a:8:1.english: "Do you think that the host imposed a vow upon the guest? No, the guest imposed a vow upon the host. He said to him: 'Do you invite me?' He said to him: 'Yes'" - Explanation: "Yes, I want to invite you." And the guest said to the host: "Vow upon yourself that you will invite me." And he vowed — explanation: the host vowed and said, "[Let] produce be konam [forbidden] to me if I do not invite you." And [these] are not vows of exhortation, because [the category of] vows of exhortation applies only where the guest refuses and the host urges him and exhorts him to eat from his [food]; but here, there is no need to exhort the guest to eat, for on the contrary, the guest requests of the host that he vow regarding this, that he will invite him.

Tosafot on Nedarim 24a:9:1.hebrew: יתר על כן אמר ר' אליעזר ב"י ואוכל עמו פת חמה - וא"ת: מאי "יתר על כן"? י"ל דהכי קאמר: אע"ג דשייך לומר "לאו כלבא אנא". וא"ת: והאמר לעיל דלא הוי זירוזין היכא דשייך לומר "לאו כלבא אנא"?! לכן נראה דאמר ליה: "קונם שאי אתה נהנה ממני לעולם אם אי אתה אוכל היום פת חמה", והשתא לא שייך טעמא ד"לאו כלבא אנא". ואשמעינן דאע"ג דפי' לו פת חמה וכוס של חמין — דמקפיד הוא טפי, וסד"א דמתכוין לנדר — אפ"ה שרי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 24a:9:1.english: Further, Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov said: ... and he eats hot bread with him - And if you ask: What is [the meaning of] "Further"? One can answer that this is what it means: [It is a vow of exhortation] even though it is applicable to say, "I am not a dog." And if you ask: Did [the Gemara] not say above that it is not [a vow of] exhortation wherever it is applicable to say, "I am not a dog"? Therefore, it appears [that the case is] where he said to him, "Konam that you shall not benefit from me forever if you do not eat hot bread today," and now the rationale of "I am not a dog" does not apply. And it teaches us that even though he specified to him "hot bread and a cup of hot [water]" — where he is more insistent, and you might have thought that he intends [an actual] vow — even so, it is permitted.
